stem: When calling the Child Protection Helpline, why is it recommended to use simple language rather than complex medical jargon?

options.text: Staff taking the call may have very little health background.
The call is being transcribed by an automated system.
Legal requirements forbid the use of medical terms in reports.
It speeds up the electronic filing process.

explanation: Clear communication ensures the risk is understood and the report isn't closed prematurely due to misunderstanding.
rationale: Consider the perspective of the person on the other end of the phone line.

optionExplanations.A: Clear communication ensures the risk is understood and the report isn't closed prematurely due to misunderstanding.
optionExplanations.B: The lecture notes that a person takes the information, but their background is not necessarily in healthcare.
optionExplanations.C: There is no such legal prohibition; simple language is just a practical recommendation for clarity.
optionExplanations.D: While it might be faster, the primary concern is the staff's ability to accurately interpret the level of risk.

source.hint: Consider the perspective of the person on the other end of the phone line.
